chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abu Shibl, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not see anything equal to visiting the believer except feeding him, and it is a right upon Allah that He feeds the one who feeds a believer from the food of Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for feeding a believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the spiritual status of visiting a fellow believer (ziyarat al-mu'min) to be nearly equivalent to feeding them, emphasizing the tangible social and spiritual bonds of the community. He further articulates a unique theological concept where Allah assumes a 'right' (haqqan ala Allah) to reward the one who feeds a believer with sustenance from Paradise, highlighting the reciprocal nature of divine grace and human kindness. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on communal solidarity and the merit of nurturing relationships with the faithful as a means of attaining divine proximity.
